commons:153352956.summary: On a page blazing with bands of yellow and orange, the white Lamb stands on a stylised Mount Zion, a mound of interlocking arches, bearing a tall cross. Around him rows of haloed figures raise stringed instruments in praise, while above a register of seated figures with books flanks winged heavenly beings. Painted by Maius for a copy of Beatus of Liébana's Commentary on the Apocalypse, the miniature turns Revelation's vision of the redeemed singing a new song before the Lamb into a jubilant pattern of colour and rhythm.
facts: The Morgan Beatus (MS M.644) was illuminated by the painter Maius (Magius), who is named in a colophon on folio 293 and a memento on folio 233.
It is one of the oldest surviving illustrated Beatus manuscripts and one of the earliest works of so-called Mozarabic art.
The Latin caption above the musicians reads, in substance, 'the Lamb standing on Mount Sion, and the hundred and forty-four thousand holding harps' (Agnus stans in monte Sion ... habentes citharas).
commons:153352956.notes: Commons gives 925–968; the Morgan Library dates the manuscript c. 945 (Wikipedia's link to the Morgan's record reads 'San Salvador de Tábara, ca. 945', while the Wikipedia text associates it with San Miguel de Escalada) — place given as León (kingdom) for that reason. The Lamb is the Apocalypse's image of Christ.
